source.title: The Surprising Harmfulness of Benign Overfitting for Adversarial Robustness

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent cutoff or corruption affecting the reported results.
record.tranche_reason: The paper theoretically studies generalization after fitting noisy training data, using standard-risk measures in linear regression and a two-layer NTK model. It does not test the specific settings or measures in the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results about standard risk after fitting noisy data. Its adversarial-risk results concern a separate robustness measure and are not cataloged as test-gap results. It does not test random-label versus natural-label classification, width sweeps, convolutional architecture, optimizer comparisons, batch size, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples.
record.test_reason: The study proves conditional results about benign overfitting and adversarial robustness in regression. None tests V1–V8: fitting additive noise with vanishing excess risk does not establish V1's random-label versus natural-label comparison, and the NTK width assumptions do not establish V2's improvement with increasing width.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. Under the stated conditions, ridgeless linear regression and a two-layer NTK gradient-descent solution have vanishing standard excess risk but diverging adversarial risk despite a robust target. The ridge result specifically establishes a trade-off between standard-risk convergence rate and bounded adversarial risk; it does not establish unconditional incompatibility of small absolute risks.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses theoretical linear regression and NTK analyses with standard-risk and adversarial-risk bounds, rather than the listed empirical interventions and test-error measures.
record.method_sensitivity: The conclusions are conditional on the stated data-noise, covariance-eigenvalue, benign-overfitting, and (for the ridge trade-off) parameter conditions; the paper also notes that truncation can yield both well-behaved standard risk and robustness in some regimes.

fits_no_version.finding: Under specified covariance, signal and noise assumptions, interpolating linear regression and a two-layer NTK gradient-descent solution have vanishing standard excess risk.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Exact fitting of noisy regression data can coexist with vanishing standard excess risk under suitable distributional and estimator assumptions.

fits_no_version.finding: Under additional trade-off conditions, every ridge parameter yields divergence of the sum of normalized standard risk and scaled adversarial risk.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In specified benign-overfitting regression regimes, ridge regularization cannot preserve the ridgeless standard-risk convergence rate while keeping adversarial risk bounded.

record.problems: The evidence is theoretical and conditional on distributional and asymptotic assumptions. The NTK extension requires high-dimensional conditions, and the paper identifies relaxing one such condition as future work. No empirical natural-label classification train-test gap is measured.
record.rows_left_out: Adversarial-risk-only conclusions and detailed bounds were not extracted as separate rows because adversarial risk is not the standard train-test gap named by the claim. Theorem 2 is retained as one combined trade-off result.

untested.parts: The same architecture and recipe fitting fixed random labels and generalizing on natural labels, with chance held-out accuracy on random labels.
Test-error changes as network width increases beyond the width needed to interpolate.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove the penalty.
Dropout effects on held-out error across training-set sizes and regularization recipes.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T2 classification conflicts with its correctly unlinked rows. Adversarial vulnerability does not challenge any listed version, and no version-level verdict is warranted. Adversarial-risk-only results were explicitly declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: No comparison of fitting random labels with generalizing on natural labels; no CIFAR-10 or ImageNet classification.
No width sweep around the interpolation threshold or test-error measurements across widths.
No convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier comparison.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison.
No batch-size comparison or epoch-budget intervention.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or ranking against other generalization measures.
No removal of memorized training examples or retraining comparison.

rows.subject: min-norm estimator θ̂λ |λ=0
rows.size_stated: Overparameterized linear model; dimension p; no specific size stated.
rows.operation_detail: Fit the linear regression model with the ridgeless estimator (λ=0) in the benign-overfitting regime.

conditions.value: i.i.d. linear regression with sub-Gaussian design and noise σ² = ω(λk*+1 rk*/n)

rows.uncertainty: Convergence in probability; theorem also gives high-probability bounds.
rows.note: The paper characterizes standard excess mean squared error, not classification test error or a measured train-test error gap.
rows.check: The stated convergence matches Theorem 1, but measures none of V1–V8. The standard-risk consistency component is explicitly credited to prior work; it should not be presented as a new standalone discovery of this study.

rows.subject: ridge regression estimator θ̂λ
rows.size_stated: Overparameterized linear model; dimension p; no specific size stated.
rows.operation_detail: Fit ridge regression across regularization parameters λ ≥ 0 under the benign-overfitting and trade-off conditions.

conditions.value: i.i.d. linear regression with sub-Gaussian design and noise σ² = ω(λk*+1 rk*/n)

rows.measure: Combined standard-risk and adversarial-risk trade-off: Rstd(θ̂λ)/(||θ||² Rstd(θ̂λ |λ=0)) + Radvα(θ̂λ)/α²
rows.uncertainty: Convergence in probability; theorem states high-probability bounds.
rows.note: The combined quantity does not isolate a training-test error gap; adversarial risk is a distinct robustness measure.
rows.check: The formula matches Theorem 2 but measures none of V1–V8. Its standard-risk term is normalized by ridgeless risk and parameter norm: the theorem concerns preserving a convergence rate while controlling adversarial risk, rather than ruling out simultaneously small absolute risks.

rows.subject: gradient descent solution ŵ in two-layer NTK model
rows.size_stated: Two-layer network with m neurons; p = o(m¹ᐟ²)
rows.stage_stated: NTK regime; gradient descent run to its convergence point with a small learning rate
rows.operation_detail: Run gradient descent on least-squares loss in the NTK regime to the stated minimum-norm solution.

conditions.value: i.i.d. high-dimensional sub-Gaussian inputs with slow-decaying covariance eigenvalues

rows.uncertainty: Theorem 3 gives a high-probability bound; Corollary 4 states convergence in probability.
rows.note: The result is for a theoretical NTK model and standard risk, not natural-label classification accuracy or an explicitly measured train-test gap.
rows.check: The stated convergence matches Corollary 4 but measures none of V1–V8. Width is constrained to ensure the NTK regime; there is no comparison showing that further widening lowers test error.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
